comment: Anankos Sim Lab technique library. SIMULATION ONLY: every effect mutates in-memory simulated state. 'requires' gates the kill chain: none | it | it_or_exposed | exposed | ot. 'stage': it_access -> pivot -> ot_access -> impact. 'domain': enterprise (IT ATT&CK) | ics (ATT&CK for ICS).

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Exploit an internet-facing enterprise application (VPN, web portal, email) to gain a foothold on the business/IT network.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Trick a staff member into running attacker code or giving up credentials, establishing an IT-network foothold.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.description: Abuse an exposed remote-access service (RDP, VPN, Citrix) to log into the enterprise network.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Use legitimate (stolen or leaked) credentials to access the enterprise network as a trusted user.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.description: Pivot from the compromised IT network across the IT/OT boundary into the control network, gaining OT access.

techniques.name: Trusted Relationship (Telecom Provider Pivot)
techniques.description: Abuse the compromised telecom carrier's trusted connection to a subscriber utility: because the provider carries that utility's SCADA/comms, control of the provider opens an OT path into it. Requires the telecom provider's OT to be compromised first.

techniques.name: Internet Accessible Device
techniques.description: Connect directly to a control device that is reachable from the internet. Only viable where the 'internet exposed' finding is set.

techniques.name: Default Credentials
techniques.description: Authenticate to an engineering interface with factory-default credentials. Needs network reach: an IT foothold or an internet-exposed device.

techniques.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
techniques.description: Exploit an exposed OT service to gain control of a facility's control network. Needs an IT foothold or an internet-exposed device.

techniques.name: Modify Parameter
techniques.description: Change a device setpoint or configuration parameter to drive the process out of its safe band.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.description: Issue an unauthorized control command to an actuator (open a breaker, stop a pump, force a transfer switch).

techniques.name: Manipulation of Control
techniques.description: Take direct control of a process actuator, overriding normal automatic regulation.

techniques.name: Manipulate I/O Image
techniques.description: Alter the I/O image the controller reads so logic acts on falsified field values while the physical process diverges.

techniques.name: Spoof Reporting Message
techniques.description: Falsify the value reported to the operator HMI so the control room sees normal readings while the real value diverges.

techniques.name: Denial of View
techniques.description: Blind the operator by denying the control-room view of the process.

techniques.name: Denial of Service
techniques.description: Flood or crash a device's communications so it can no longer respond to commands or protective logic.

techniques.name: Device Restart/Shutdown
techniques.description: Force a controller or actuator to restart or shut down, dropping the process it governs.

techniques.name: Loss of Availability
techniques.description: Render a control function unavailable, stopping the process or service it provides.

techniques.name: Loss of Control
techniques.description: Deny operators the ability to control the process, leaving it in whatever state the attacker set.

techniques.name: Loss of Safety
techniques.description: Defeat or disable a safety instrumented function so the process can reach an unsafe state without protective intervention.
